Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test: org.apache.commons.compress.utils.ChecksumCalculatingInputStreamTest.testClassInstantiationWithParameterBeingNullThrowsNullPointerExceptionOne expects a NullPointerException when constructing ChecksumCalculatingInputStream with both parameters null:
  - new ChecksumCalculatingInputStream(null, null)
- Implementation of the constructor:
  - org.apache.commons.compress.utils.ChecksumCalculatingInputStream.ChecksumCalculatingInputStream(java.util.zip.Checksum, java.io.InputStream) simply assigns the parameters to fields without any null checks:
    - lines 33–39: this.checksum = checksum; this.in = in;
  - Therefore, constructing with null arguments does not throw immediately, causing the test that expects an immediate NPE to fail.
- Downstream dereferences confirm latent NPEs:
  - getValue() calls checksum.getValue() without checking for null (lines 95–97), which throws NullPointerException if checksum is null.
  - read(byte[], int, int) calls in.read(...) and then checksum.update(...) without checks (lines 73–79), which will also NPE if either field is null.
- Current bug report corroborates this: “NullPointerException defect in ChecksumCalculatingInputStream#getValue()” indicates callers are seeing NPEs from getValue() when checksum is null. This is a direct consequence of the constructor not validating inputs and allowing null to be stored.
- Root cause:
  - The constructor lacks argument validation and allows null values for both the Checksum and InputStream fields. This violates the test’s expectation that null arguments should be rejected at construction time and leads to later NPEs in getValue() and read().

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
